memory.content: The user prefers responses in Spanish.
Weekday business Gmail digests at 11:30 AM and 5:30 PM local time, prioritizing a named VIP client domain, plus alerts for bank and other priority clients.
Highest-priority client mail: alert immediately with a short Spanish summary when new messages arrive from that domain.
Invoice Drive filing convention: year folder → Spanish month folders → PDF and XML subfolders.

skills.name: Resolve all-day event time
skills.description: Use when listing today's agenda or digests and an event shows as all-day — resolve the real local start time.
skills.content:
---
name: Resolve all-day event time
description: >-
  Use when listing today's agenda or digests and an event shows as all-day —
  resolve the real local start time.
---
When listing today's (or this week's) events, never leave a livestream, webinar, meetup, or timed show as bare "all day" if the user is likely to ask what time it is.

## When to use
- Listing "hoy", "mañana", or the day's agenda from a calendar or inbox digest
- An event comes back as all-day, date-only, or without a clock time
- The title or description hints at a live stream, webinar, conference session, concert, or "a las …"

## Steps
1. Pull the event details (description, location, conference link, attachments, related email if you already have it).
2. Look for an explicit clock time in local terms.
3. Convert to the user's local timezone and state that clock time in the list, not only "todo el día".
4. If several candidate times appear, pick the start time of the live session.
5. If no clock time exists after a real look, say "todo el día / sin hora publicada" — do not invent one.

skills.description: Use when designing or creating a new Grok Bot.
skills.content:
---
name: Design a Grok Bot
description: Use when designing or creating a new Grok Bot.
---
Create the bot. A bot is four fields: one job, anti-jobs, voice, wake. Name is short; description carries all four. CreateAgent takes name and description only; verify the live profile after create. Ask only preference questions no experiment can settle.

routines.name: Priority client mail alert
routines.description: Weekday daytime check for new VIP-client and bank mail; alert immediately with a Spanish summary, stay silent when nothing is new.
routines.content:
Watch the connected business Gmail for NEW emails from the configured highest-priority client domain that have not been alerted yet.

For each new matching email: read enough to write a short Spanish summary (from, subject, 2–4 sentence gist, any clear ask, amount, or deadline). Notify the user right away with that summary and tell them to review it in that inbox. Do not send or reply unless they ask.

Also briefly flag any other priority bank/client mail found in the same pass AFTER the VIP client, with short summaries — VIP client always first.

If there is nothing new, stay completely silent.

Keep a record of already-alerted message ids to avoid duplicates. If Gmail auth fails repeatedly, pause this routine and tell the user to reconnect.

Fill-ins: VIP client domain; bank/priority domains; alerted-ids store path.

Fires on:
- cron `16 9-18 * * 1-5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: Morning Gmail digest
routines.description: Weekday 11:30 AM local Spanish digest of business Gmail, VIP client first, then banks, then notable rest.
routines.content:
Produce the morning business Gmail digest for the user in Spanish.

Cover new/unread or arrived this morning up to now. Structure:
1) VIP client domain FIRST — each with short summary
2) Other priority (banks / listed clients)
3) Rest of notable inbox (brief bullets; skip pure noise)

Notify the user with this digest. If the inbox is empty of anything worth mentioning, stay silent.

Fill-ins: Gmail account label; VIP domain; bank/priority domains.

Fires on:
- cron `30 11 * * 1-5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.description: Weekday 5:30 PM local Spanish digest of mail since the morning digest, same priority order.
routines.content:

1) VIP client domain FIRST — each with short summary
2) Other priority (banks / listed clients)
3) Rest of notable inbox (brief bullets; skip pure noise)

Notify the user with this digest. If nothing worth mentioning, stay silent.

Fill-ins: Gmail account label; VIP domain; bank/priority domains.

Ask the importing user for:
